item.title: Consumer Sentiment Ticked Lower in September
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index landed at 48.1 in September, down from 51.7 in August.

item.title: Durable Goods Orders Were Unchanged in August
item.content:encoded: Demand for U.S. durable goods was unchanged in August, according to Commerce Department data. Economists expected a decrease of 0.3%.

item.title: The rental market in Portland, Ore., is so depressed that high earners are paying some of the same rents as lower-income residents who qualify for subsidized housing
item.content:encoded: Rarely has the Oregon city seen such a narrow price gap between market-rate and affordable units.

item.title: Treasury Yields, Fed Rate-Hike Bets Rise After Strong U.S. Jobs Data
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury yields jump after significantly stronger-than-expected employment data for August lifted expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the Sept. 16 meeting.

item.title: BOE Survey Points to Cooling Price Pressures
item.content:encoded: Businesses expect the prices they charge to rise by 3.8% over the coming 12 months, a decrease from the 3.9% expected in July.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Fell in August
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell 2.6% in August to 1.275 million. Economists expected a reading of 1.3 million and for starts to rise 4.9% over the month.

item.title: Eurozone Consumer Sentiment Knocked by Surging Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: The European Commission’s flash consumer-confidence indicator for the 21-nation currency area fell 1.0 point to minus 16.5 in September.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Has Dropped in August, per Michigan Survey
item.content:encoded: Consumers’ economic mood is weaker this month versus July, according to preliminary results from the University of Michigan’s monthly survey.

item.title: EU, Philippines Reach Breakthrough in Free-Trade Talks
item.content:encoded: The agreement comes as persistent geopolitical shocks and tariffs underscore the need to look for new trade partners.

item.title: The U.S. is pressuring Mexico to accept new rules for exports of AI hardware to prevent Chinese companies and other foreign firms from circumventing tariffs
item.content:encoded: Washington trade negotiators want to encourage more North American content in servers, chips and other equipment crossing America’s southern border.

item.title: German Consumer Confidence Falls to Lowest Since May on Energy Costs
item.content:encoded: Consumer confidence in Germany dropped unexpectedly sharply, dragged down by rising energy prices as tensions escalated in the Middle East.

item.title: Average 30-year mortgage rates hit 7.03% this week, the first time they have surpassed 7% since the beginning of last year
item.content:encoded: The effect of rates topping the psychologically important 7% level is rippling through the market for buyers, sellers and builders.

item.title: KB Home Cuts Margin Outlook as Housing Conditions Worsen
item.content:encoded: The homebuilder said it now expects annual gross profit margin to be 16.0% to 16.2%, down from its earlier guidance of 16.1% to 16.5%.

item.title: Dollar Jumps to 8-Week High on Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.content:encoded: The U.S. dollar rose to its highest level since late July against a basket of currencies Wednesday as markets bet on the Federal Reserve raising interest rates further.

item.title: Canada Retail Sales Recover Following First Fall of Year in July
item.content:encoded: Sales in July fell for the first time this year, declining 0.7% from the previous month to a seasonally adjusted 73.7 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.25 billion.

item.title: A broad measure of American incomes reached a record high last year as upper-income households fared well and women’s pay gained ground compared with men
item.content:encoded: The annual Census report said upper-income households fared well and women’s pay gained ground compared with men.

item.title: Last month, the U.S. added an impressive 162,000 jobs and unemployment is low, but broad economic measures might be missing how much Americans’ costs have risen—and how many of them haven’t kept up
item.content:encoded: Official data shows steady growth and low unemployment but misses how rising costs have left many Americans behind.

item.title: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans
item.content:encoded: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans.

item.title: Trump Looks to Sideline Canadian Potash With Belarusian Supply Deal
item.content:encoded: President Trump is signaling a potential agreement to purchase lower-priced potash from Belarus, a move that could challenge Canadian exporters.

item.title: Harley-Davidson dealers are worried about sticker shock for its Canadian consumers
item.content:encoded: The U.S. motorcycle maker’s politically sensitive profile keeps it on the tariff payback list.
